section_summary: This section concludes with a letter from Sumner Welles advising the President against responding to a report about the Japanese population in Mexico, partly because Guatemalan–Mexican antagonism could draw the United States into a dispute. Most remaining pages are filing or cross-reference sheets concerning Japanese commercial, engineering, mining, oil, fishing, and possible intelligence activities in Colombia, Uruguay, Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, and areas near the Panama Canal and Galápagos Islands. The section includes one substantive despatch describing four Japanese engineers' survey of the lower Patía River and the Nariño coast.

subfiles.title: Letter from Sumner Welles concerning Des Portes' report on Japanese residents in Mexico
subfiles.to: The President of the United States
subfiles.about: Welles advises that Des Portes' letter should be filed without reply unless a forthcoming War Department report materially changes the estimated Japanese population in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Welles states that American and Mexican sources support the War Department's estimate that no more than approximately 12,000 Japanese reside in Mexico. He suggests seeking an authoritative survey only if the War Department's further report shows a material increase. He warns that instructions to Des Portes might have unfortunate consequences because the Ubico government in Guatemala is strongly antagonistic toward Mexico and might welcome a U.S.–Mexican dispute.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 2374: Japanese activities in Colombia
subfiles.about: The note records a report that four Japanese engineers surveyed the lower Patía River and the coast near Sanquianga.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet cross-references Despatch No. 2374 to file 894.20210/17. It summarizes information that four Japanese engineers made a thorough survey of the lower Patía River and the neighboring Sanquianga coast.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2374: Japanese activities in Colombia
subfiles.about: The despatch reports that four Japanese engineers surveyed the lower Patía River and the Nariño coast near Sanquianga.
subfiles.summary: A representative of the Chocó-Pacífico company, recently returned from Barbacoas, reported that four Japanese engineers had thoroughly surveyed the lower reaches of the Patía River and the coast near Sanquianga. The writer had not recently discussed Japanese activities with Colombian officials because Colonel León Gómez had left for the United States and the Foreign Office had changed its Secretary General. The badly damaged conclusion indicates an intention to raise the subject when a favorable opportunity arose.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 4667: Japanese activities in Uruguay
subfiles.about: The note records the forwarding of a memorandum reviewing Japanese activities in Uruguay during the quarter ending December 1, 1938.
subfiles.summary: The filing sheet cross-references Despatch No. 4667 to another decimal-file location. It states that Third Secretary Ragonier prepared the enclosed quarterly review of Japanese activities in Uruguay.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 2510: Japanese activities in Colombia
subfiles.about: The note summarizes Japanese mineral exploration in Putumayo and Colombian resistance to Japanese concessions and yarn imports.
subfiles.summary: Japanese mining engineers, probably Shiro Ohmachi and Hiroju Takahashi, were reported to be examining mineral prospects in the Putumayo District. Colombia's Minister of National Economy reportedly told an American businessman that obstacles would be placed in the way of Japanese concession seekers. The Exchange Control Board had also refused import licenses for Japanese yarn because the applicable quota was exhausted.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 7991: Japanese activities in Latin America
subfiles.about: The note records a report that Namagati contracted with Galino Reyes to drill oil wells on Lot 6 at Concepción, Mexico.
subfiles.summary: The filing sheet summarizes an item in El Aguila's report of December 19, 1938. It states that the Japanese individual Namagati signed a contract with Mexican contractor Galino Reyes for drilling as many as twenty oil wells per year on Lot 6 at Concepción.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 838: Japanese activities in Guatemala
subfiles.about: The note reports no significant Japanese activity in Guatemala during the three months ending February 28, 1939.
subfiles.summary: The report found practically no commerce between Guatemala and Japan. Diplomatic relations were described as largely nonexistent, in part because Guatemala lacked a resident Japanese colony.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 500: Japanese activities in El Salvador
subfiles.about: The note describes brief visits to El Salvador by Limoda of the Japanese Fisheries Company and a representative of the Asahi Shimbun.
subfiles.summary: Little Japanese activity was reported in El Salvador during the preceding three months. Limoda, head of the Japanese Fisheries Company, spent three days there in January, and an Asahi Shimbun representative soon followed for a two-day stay before continuing to other Central American capitals. Neither visit was believed to have an official purpose.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 565: Japanese activities in Uruguay
subfiles.about: The note records the forwarding of a memorandum reviewing Japanese activities in Uruguay for the quarter ending March 1, 1939.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet identifies Despatch No. 565 from Uruguay. Its enclosure reviewed Japanese activities during the quarterly period ending March 1, 1939.

subfiles.title: Document file note for Despatch No. 36: Japanese activities near the Panama Canal
subfiles.about: The note records Braden's conversation with the French Minister about Japanese activities near the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: This confidential filing sheet concerns Japanese activities in the vicinity of the Panama Canal. It identifies a conversation between Braden and the French Minister as the subject of Despatch No. 36.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note: German and Japanese activities in and near the American republics
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a Navy Department letter submitting two memoranda on German and Japanese activities in and near the American republics.
subfiles.summary: The note points researchers to the original Navy Department letter in file 862.20210/1642. That letter transmitted copies of two memoranda concerning German and Japanese activities in or near the American republics.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note: Japanese oil concessions in the Isthmus
subfiles.from: State Department, Division of American Republics (Bursley)
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a memorandum reporting that Japanese interests were about to receive oil concessions in the Isthmus of Panama.
subfiles.summary: The note concerns Japanese activities in Latin America and directs researchers to a memorandum in file 800.20210/355. Its brief subject description states that Japanese interests were about to obtain oil concessions in the Isthmus.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note: Japanese activities in South American waters
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a report concerning Japanese activities near the Galápagos Islands and possible wartime danger to the tuna fleet.
subfiles.summary: The referenced letter transmitted a report from a Bureau of Fisheries agent in California about the tuna fleet's potential exposure to belligerents. It commented on Japanese activities near the Galápagos Islands and reported the seizure of stores and fuel from a fishing vessel. The sheet directs researchers to file 812.628/575 for the original letter.
